prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell) serves Meridian International Airport, Harbor East Airport, North Valley Airport, Lakeside Regional Airport, Southport Airport; statutory/local authority remains.
Elements/flows: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone) receives filed flights through Flight Data Exchange, compares Airline Interface Adapter schedules; Flight Intent Message updates override materially differing schedules. Forecasts use conformance, rotations, banks. Capacity Assessment Module combines forecasts/Airport Capacity Plan, tests Airport Acceptance Rate feasibility. Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard) normalizes external/local meteorology. Sector Load Monitor supplies airspace demand. Capacity incorporates traffic, resources, constraints, weather, continuously updated.
Other elements: Slot Allocation Engine; Airport CDM Portal; Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Alert Distribution Hub; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service; Business Rules Registry; Time Synchronization Service.
Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin) owns baseline/alignment, chairs tactical checkpoints, authorizes measures when declared/observed capacity diverges; Airline Operations Coordinator; Network Operations Liaison (compatibility, Collaborative Decision Log); Aircraft Operator Representative (feasible commitments); Slot Coordinator (policy; no baseline binding Calculated Takeoff Time); Tower Supervisor (sequencing/configuration, Runway Inspection Note); Ramp Control Lead; Airport Duty Manager; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Handling Resource Planner; Deicing Coordinator (winter readiness/metering/throughput advice); Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot, forecasts/triggers); Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison (availability, warns Copperfin); Emergency Response Coordinator (mandatory safety/security/emergency-impact escalation); Data Governance Steward (verifies synchronized decision/acknowledgement/exception auditing); System Support Engineer (degradation/interface/exchange escalation).
Indicators: North Runway Meter; South Runway Meter; East Apron Sensor; West Apron Sensor; Gate Conflict Detector.
Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State; Slot Compliance State.
Accountable roles authorize metering/regulation; outputs visible on Common Situation Display; confirm tactical-period decisions/unresolved issues reach warehouse for Post Operations Report. Baseline reviews include Ground Delay Program, Tactical Regulation Proposal; metering estimates Target Off Block Time sensitivity.

New part:
S108: The Weather Ingest Gateway accepts aviation forecasts, radar-derived precipitation fields, lightning alerts, wind forecasts, ceiling and visibility forecasts, and runway condition weather inputs from approved sources.
S109: Each weather feed is checked for source identity, issue time, valid time, spatial reference, and unit consistency before it is made available to the Regional Flow Platform.
S110: The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock used to compare forecast issue times with operational decision times.
S111: When a forecast product arrives late or fails validation, the Weather Ingest Gateway marks the feed as degraded rather than silently excluding it from the operational picture.
S112: The Meteorology Briefing Officer reviews degraded weather inputs when they affect capacity assumptions for the next planning period.
S113: Weather impacts are translated into capacity modifiers for runway configuration, arrival spacing, departure spacing, surface movement constraints, and approach sector availability.
S114: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter receive runway-specific capacity values after the Capacity Assessment Module applies the current wind, visibility, and precipitation assumptions.
S115: Surface constraints from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor are correlated with weather-driven taxi speed assumptions before the Ramp Movement Board is updated.
S116: The Airport Duty Manager may request a manual capacity review when local observations differ materially from the automated weather interpretation.
S117: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Common Situation Display to compare forecast demand, assessed capacity, and any active Ground Delay Program effects in one operational view.
S118: Forecast confidence is recorded as a confidence class, a probability value where provided by the source, a valid time range, and the forecast horizon used for the calculation.
S119: The confidence record also stores the originating feed, the processing time, the transformation version, and any manual override applied by the Meteorology Briefing Officer.
S120: Low-confidence weather forecasts remain visible to users, but the Capacity Assessment Module flags the associated capacity values as provisional.
S121: When confidence decreases below the configured threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Airline Operations Coordinator that the capacity picture may change.
S122: All forecast confidence changes, feed quality changes, and capacity recalculations are written to the Collaborative Decision Log with synchronized timestamps.
S123: The Audit Event Ledger retains the trace from incoming forecast product to capacity value so that the Performance Analytics Warehouse can reconstruct the decision basis after operations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
